project: Project Q - IBM Quantum Qiskit Fall Fest 2026

project_owner_review_summary.notes: The project owner has individually reviewed the proposed choices and endorsed D5 (L=1), D6 (polarity: positive=VEB, negative=Normal), and D9 (MSE/Brier). These represent individual owner selections and do NOT constitute formal NEXUS-OPS team consensus. All decisions remain PROPOSED_NOT_TEAM_APPROVED pending full team sign-off.

decisions.name: Qubit count
decisions.purpose: Provide a 1:1 direct mapping from the 6 engineered biomedical features to individual qubits.
technical_advantages: Retains all six physiological feature dimensions without lossy dimensionality reduction (e.g., PCA).
Theoretical state space dimension is 2^6 = 64, computationally lightweight for classical statevector simulation.
Allows local observable readout per feature domain.
limitations_and_risks: Higher qubit requirement than compressed 3-qubit re-uploading architectures.
Physical NISQ implementation requires maintaining gate fidelity across all 6 physical qubits.
verification_requirements: Verify that qubit index mapping strictly preserves feature column order (pre_rr -> q0, post_rr -> q1, qrs_rms -> q2, qrs_duration -> q3, p2p_amplitude -> q4, spectral_ratio -> q5).
Verify quantum register allocation in QuantumCircuit(6) once constructed.

decisions.name: Feature encoding
decisions.purpose: Encode normalized continuous features into single-qubit state rotations using the Ry basis.
technical_advantages: Theoretical depth O(1) circuit with exactly zero two-qubit entangling gates in the encoding stage.
Generates purely real probability amplitudes, avoiding unnecessary phase complexity.
Rotation angles naturally span [0, pi], matching the preprocessed feature scaling interval.
limitations_and_risks: Creates an unentangled product state at the encoding boundary; feature interactions must be learned solely by the downstream ansatz.
Crucial theoretical distinction: RY angle encoding does NOT make the VQC equivalent to classical logistic regression once followed by multi-qubit entanglement.
verification_requirements: Verify feature inputs are strictly bounded in [0, pi] and clipped against out-of-range test values.
Verify parameter vector binding order during Qiskit circuit evaluation.

decisions.name: Ansatz
decisions.purpose: Parameterize the quantum state using alternating layers of parameterized Ry gates and fixed entanglers.
technical_advantages: Preserves real-valued quantum statevectors (amplitudes in R^64), halving parameter count compared to SU(2) rotations.
Directly compatible with Qiskit 2.x circuit library and standard hardware native gate sets.
Compact parameter space accelerates classical optimization convergence.
limitations_and_risks: Restricts variational state exploration to the real sub-manifold of Hilbert space, ignoring complex phase degrees of freedom.
Expressivity may be bounded compared to full EfficientSU2 if complex interference is needed.
verification_requirements: Verify that gate construction matches standard RealAmplitudes parameter ordering.
Verify that no unexpected complex unitaries are introduced.

decisions.name: Entanglement
decisions.purpose: Introduce quantum correlations between adjacent qubits via nearest-neighbor CNOT gates.
technical_advantages: Minimal two-qubit gate count: theoretical expectation is n - 1 = 5 CNOT gates for 6 qubits.
Directly matches linear physical topology on superconducting processors without requiring SWAP overhead.
Significantly lower gate error accumulation than all-to-all entanglement (which requires 15 CNOTs theoretically).
limitations_and_risks: Information propagation between non-adjacent qubits (e.g., q0 and q5) is indirect and weak across a single layer.
Entanglement structure depends heavily on the ordering of input features assigned to qubits.
verification_requirements: Verify CNOT directionality and pair order: (0, 1), (1, 2), (2, 3), (3, 4), (4, 5).
Verify that adjacent qubit pairs correlate clinically meaningful feature interactions.

decisions.name: Ansatz repetitions
decisions.purpose: Set the repetition depth of the parameterized entangling block to a single layer as the primary baseline.
technical_advantages: Yields a compact theoretical parameter vector of 12 trainable parameters (6 initial Ry + 6 post-entanglement Ry).
Low circuit depth minimizes barren plateau risks and optimization landscape ruggedness.
Fast classical simulation runtime during multi-seed training.
limitations_and_risks: Underfitting risk: a single layer may have insufficient expressive power to separate complex non-linear boundary regions.
Must be benchmarked against classical logistic regression to detect underfitting.
verification_requirements: Verify theoretical parameter count equals 12 upon circuit construction.
Verify training loss converges and evaluate whether L=2 is warranted as an ablation study.

decisions.name: Measurement
decisions.verdict: ACCEPTABLE FOR BASELINE (VERIFICATION REQUIRED ON POLARITY)
decisions.purpose: Measure local Pauli-Z expectation value on each qubit and average the outcomes across the register.
technical_advantages: Local observable structure provably avoids cost-function-dependent barren plateaus in shallow circuits.
Symmetric readout extracts information contributed by all six feature-encoding qubits.
Theoretical expectation value E in [-1, +1] maps linearly to probability p in [0, 1].
limitations_and_risks: Averaging across 6 qubits may dilute gradients if class separation is driven primarily by only 1-2 features.

Polarity convention: p(VEB) = (E + 1) / 2 assumes E -> +1 corresponds to VEB (class 1) and E -> -1 corresponds to Normal (class 0). The mathematical observation that E = +1 applies strictly when both input encoding angles and variational parameters are zero (x = 0, theta = 0). It does not imply that actual encoded ECG samples produce E = +1 at initialization. Initial predictions must be evaluated using the actual six scaled input features and initialized variational parameters to verify empirical polarity and alignment with dataset binary labels.
verification_requirements: Verify dataset label convention: 0 = Normal, 1 = VEB.
Verify SparsePauliOp little-endian construction for the 6 Pauli-Z terms with weight 1/6 each.
Confirm that optimization drives Normal beats toward E < 0 and VEB beats toward E > 0 without introducing ad-hoc architecture changes.

decisions.name: Optimizer
decisions.purpose: Execute classical parameter optimization using a derivative-free linear approximation method.
technical_advantages: Derivative-free approach avoids expensive numerical or parameter-shift gradient evaluations.
Fast convergence in noise-free statevector simulation.
Standard, robust implementation available via scipy.optimize.minimize without third-party dependencies.
limitations_and_risks: Gradient-free search can become trapped in shallow local minima.
COBYLA iterations and objective-function evaluations are distinct: an iteration may execute multiple function evaluations during trust-region management.
Step sizes are heuristic and can stall if initialization is near flat regions.
verification_requirements: Cap maximum iterations at 150.
Log separately: iteration_count, objective_evaluation_count, best_objective_value, termination_reason, runtime_seconds, convergence_status.

decisions.name: Initialization
decisions.purpose: Initialize variational parameters close to zero while breaking exact parameter symmetry.
technical_advantages: Starts the ansatz near the identity operation W(0) = I, avoiding random state dispersion.
Guarantees initial gradients are well-behaved and avoids barren plateau initialization regions.
Deterministic control via fixed random seed generation.
limitations_and_risks: Symmetric bounds [-0.1, 0.1] may bias initial optimization trajectories toward small rotation angles.
Performance could vary across seeds; requires multi-seed validation.
verification_requirements: Verify random number generator seed control with np.random.default_rng(seed).
Verify parameter bounds are strictly enforced at t = 0.

decisions.name: Loss
decisions.purpose: Compute mean squared error between model-predicted probabilities and binary target labels.
technical_advantages: Direct algebraic connection to Pauli expectation values: L = (1/4N) sum (E_i - (2y_i - 1))^2.
Smooth, bounded loss landscape in [0, 1] that pairs well with COBYLA.
Brier score directly evaluates probability calibration without requiring adaptive bias parameters.
limitations_and_risks: MSE gradients can flatten when predictions saturate, whereas Binary Cross-Entropy provides stronger penalization for confident errors.
May produce narrow probability distributions around 0.5 if parameters underfit.
verification_requirements: Verify loss function calculation: L = (1/N) sum (p(VEB|x_i, theta) - y_i)^2.
Verify numerical stability during optimization.

decisions.name: Simulation
decisions.purpose: Train variational parameters under exact analytical statevectors, then evaluate physical sampling robustness on the frozen model using 1,024 shots.
technical_advantages: Decouples parameter optimization from statistical shot noise during training, preventing noisy gradient stalling.
Fast, reproducible training via Qiskit 2.x StatevectorEstimator.
Allows assessing the impact of finite-shot sampling variance on frozen parameters.
limitations_and_risks: Finite-shot sampling introduces statistical variance. For S=1024 shots: theoretical standard error on E is SE(E) <= 1/sqrt(S) = 0.03125, and standard error on mapped probability p=(E+1)/2 is SE(p) <= 1/(2*sqrt(S)) = 0.015625 (approx 1.56%). This is a theoretical worst-case bound, NOT an experimentally measured variance.
Parameters converged on infinite shots may experience classification flips under shot noise if probabilities hover near 0.5.
verification_requirements: Verify StatevectorEstimator is used exclusively during training.
Verify BackendEstimatorV2 with AerSimulator(shots=1024) is used for shot-based evaluation with fixed seed.
